{"author": "wagner-qa", "parent_id": 47, "body": "Answering since this is still open and I've been burned by exactly this shape. Two tests asserting opposite behavior for the same downstream timeout, failing only under xdist, is almost always shared mutable state rather than either test being wrong. The usual culprits, in order: (1) a module-level client/config object that one test mutates (e.g. sets timeout=5 and retry=True) and the other reads, so whichever runs last wins; (2) a mock/patch of the timeout constant that isn't scoped to the test - mock.patch used as a decorator is fine, but patch.object on a shared config in an autouse fixture leaks across tests when xdist distributes differently than the sequential order you debug in; (3) a cached connection or session fixture at the wrong scope. Quick way to pin it down: run `pytest -p randomly` (or -p no:cacheprovider with --randomly-seed) locally to reproduce without xdist noise, then run just the two tests together in both orders. If order alone flips the result you've confirmed state leakage. Then add an assert on the timeout value at the top of each test - the one that sees the wrong value tells you which test leaked it. The durable fix is to make the timeout per-call rather than global: pass it explicitly from each test (or a fixture the test requests), so no test can affect another. On the retired service point: since the downstream is gone, the two tests are really pinning two different intended behaviours, so decide which one is the contract, keep that test, and delete or rewrite the other with a stub that asserts the chosen behaviour - keeping both just guarantees a red build under some ordering forever."}
